The input is DIA-NN's precursor report: one row per precursor ion per run. limpa is built for this
level. It reads the report, keeps confidently identified precursors, and later quantifies each
protein from its precursors with a model of which ones go undetected. This step reads the report,
picks one injection per biopsy, applies limpa's two identity filters and saves the precursor
matrix. Nothing is normalised and nothing is filtered on missing values; limpa models both.

## Packages

limpa supplies the reader and the filters, limma the `EList` they return and the density plot.
`readDIANN()` reads Parquet through the nanoparquet package, which must be installed.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(limma)
library(limpa)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
stopifnot(requireNamespace("nanoparquet", quietly = TRUE))
inputs <- c(
  report = "00_Setup/Input/report.parquet",
  metadata = "00_Setup/Input/metadata.csv"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
out <- here("01_Processing", "01_Precursors", "c_data")
packageVersion("limpa")
```

## Read the report

`readDIANN()` (limpa) reads the Parquet report into a precursor-by-run matrix of log2
`Precursor.Normalised` intensities, `NA` where a precursor was not detected in a run. It keeps a
precursor in a run only when its q-values pass 0.01. Which q-values depends on the search: with
match-between-runs (MBR), DIA-NN builds one library from all runs and searches each run against it,
and limpa's vignette then filters on `Q.Value`, `Lib.Q.Value` and `Lib.PG.Q.Value`. This report's
library q-values differ from its global ones, consistent with an MBR search, so the MBR set is used.
(The no-MBR columns, `Global.Q.Value` and `Global.PG.Q.Value`, would keep 19,936 precursors against
22,389.)

```{r}
#| label: read
y <- readDIANN(
  paths[["report"]],
  q.columns = c("Q.Value", "Lib.Q.Value", "Lib.PG.Q.Value"), q.cutoffs = 0.01
)
c(precursors = nrow(y), runs = ncol(y), pct_missing = round(100 * mean(is.na(y$E)), 1))
```

## One injection per biopsy

The report holds 57 runs from 18 people. Some biopsies were injected twice: the second injection
carries a suffix (`r`, `rr`, `_4`, `_r`). Each run name gives the person and time point. The
analysis keeps the 16 people in `metadata.csv` and, for each biopsy, the injection that detected
the most precursors (decisions log, 2026-10-14).

```{r}
#| label: run-map
metadata <- readr::read_csv(paths[["metadata"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
run_map <- tibble(run = colnames(y), n_precursors = colSums(!is.na(y$E))) |>
  mutate(
    sample_id = sub("^JBBC_CL_(S\\d+)-(T\\d).*$", "\\1_\\2", run),
    injection = sub("^JBBC_CL_S\\d+-T\\d_?", "", run),
    in_study = sample_id %in% metadata$sample_id
  ) |>
  mutate(chosen = in_study & n_precursors == max(n_precursors), .by = sample_id) |>
  arrange(sample_id, desc(n_precursors))
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(run_map$sample_id), sum(run_map$chosen) == nrow(metadata),
  setequal(run_map$sample_id[run_map$chosen], metadata$sample_id)
)
print(run_map, n = Inf)
```

Biopsies with more than one injection, and the one kept:

```{r}
#| label: reinjections
filter(run_map, n() > 1, .by = sample_id)
```

## Keep the chosen runs

The chosen runs are renamed to their `sample_id` and matched to `metadata.csv`. A precursor
detected only in dropped runs must go: left in, it looks undetected in all 48 biopsies, which shifts
the detection curve and pulls its protein's values down (tested: values moved by up to 5 log2
units). limpa's `removeNARows()` does this, but with the installed limpa and limma it fails inside
limma's `EList` subsetting (`y[keep, , ]` passes an empty argument), so plain subsetting does it.

```{r}
#| label: subset
chosen <- filter(run_map, chosen)
y <- y[, chosen$run]
colnames(y) <- chosen$sample_id
y$targets <- metadata[match(colnames(y), metadata$sample_id), ]
y <- y[rowSums(!is.na(y$E)) > 0, ]
stopifnot(identical(y$targets$sample_id, colnames(y)))
c(precursors = nrow(y), proteins = n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group), runs = ncol(y))
```

## Identity filters

limpa's vignette applies two optional filters for easier interpretation:
`filterNonProteotypicPeptides()` drops precursors whose peptide maps to more than one protein, and
`filterCompoundProteins()` drops protein groups that name two or more proteins. Neither looks at
intensity or missing values.

```{r}
#| label: filters
before <- c(precursors = nrow(y), proteins = n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group))
y <- filterNonProteotypicPeptides(y)
y <- filterCompoundProteins(y)
after <- c(precursors = nrow(y), proteins = n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group))
filter_log <- tibble(count = names(before), before, after)
filter_log
```

Both filters remove nothing here: DIA-NN already reported proteotypic precursors only and no
protein group names two proteins. They stay as a check.

## Detection per run

Precursors and proteins detected in each kept run. limpa keeps weak runs; the comparisons
down-weight them through sample weights rather than dropping them.

```{r}
#| label: per-run
per_run <- tibble(
  sample_id = colnames(y),
  n_precursors = colSums(!is.na(y$E)),
  n_proteins = colSums(rowsum(1 * !is.na(y$E), y$genes$Protein.Group) > 0)
) |>
  left_join(select(metadata, sample_id, group, timepoint), by = "sample_id") |>
  arrange(n_precursors)
print(per_run, n = 6)
summary(per_run$n_precursors)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-per-run
#| fig-cap: "Precursors detected per kept run, by time point and group."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3
ggplot(per_run, aes(timepoint, n_precursors, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "precursors detected", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

## Intensities per biopsy

limpa adds no normalisation: it uses DIA-NN's `Precursor.Normalised`. If that worked, every
biopsy's distribution of detected log2 intensities sits in the same place. limma's
`plotDensities()` draws one curve per biopsy; a shifted curve would mean the normalisation failed
for that run. Thin runs detect fewer faint precursors, so their curves start further right.

```{r}
#| label: fig-densities
#| fig-cap: "Detected log2 precursor intensity per biopsy (limma's plotDensities)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
plotDensities(y, legend = FALSE, main = "")
round(summary(apply(y$E, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)), 2)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  ncol(y) == 48, !anyDuplicated(colnames(y)), all(rowSums(!is.na(y$E)) > 0),
  !anyNA(y$genes$Protein.Group)
)
```

## Summary

`r nrow(y)` precursors from `r n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group)` proteins in `r ncol(y)` biopsies;
`r round(100 * mean(is.na(y$E)), 1)`% of the matrix is missing, and limpa models every missing
value in the next step.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(y, file.path(out, "precursors.rds"))
readr::write_csv(run_map, file.path(out, "run_map.csv"))
write_workbook(
  list(run_map = run_map, filter_log = filter_log, per_run = per_run),
  c(
    "Every run in the report: biopsy, injection, precursors detected, and whether it was kept.",
    "Precursors and proteins before and after the identity filters.",
    "Precursors and proteins detected in each kept run."
  ),
  file.path(out, "precursors.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
